headline: 7, including Obaidul Quader, sentenced to death for crimes against humanity
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced seven high-ranking members of the banned Awami League and its affiliates to death for atrocities during the July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has sentenced seven individuals, including banned Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader, Joint General Secretary A.F.M. Bahauddin Nasim, and former State Minister for Information Mohammad E. Arafat, to death for crimes against humanity.

Other convicts include Jubo League President Sheikh Fazle Shams Porosh, General Secretary Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain, and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Inan.

The verdict was delivered Tuesday at 12:15 PM by a three-member judicial panel led by Chairman Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, alongside judges Mohammad Manjurul Bashid and Nur Mohammad Shahriyar Kabir.
All seven accused have been fugitives since the beginning of the case. The tribunal formally took the charges into account on December 18 last year and issued arrest warrants for them.
The prosecution's case began with an opening statement on February 17, following the framing of charges on January 22. Final arguments were presented between August 4 and August 12.
The prosecution alleged that the defendants coordinated, incited, and gave orders to suppress the July-August movement through provocative speeches and strategic planning.
It was further alleged that they played key roles in armed attacks, severe repression, and the control of media to stifle the the uprising.
The tribunal found that these actions led to widespread killings, attempted murders, and extensive violence across the country, which are punishable as crimes against humanity.
caption:
Death sentences for 7 top leaders, including Obaidul Quader, for crimes against humanity.

All seven accused have been fugitives since the beginning of the case. The tribunal formally took the charges into account on December 18 last year and issued arrest warrants for them.

headline_marked: 1,733 hospitalised as [[8 more die of dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 1,733 hospitalised as 8 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The daily case count has hit a record high for the year, while the death toll reaches 157 total fatalities according to the DGHS.
details: At least eight dengue patients died in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am yesterday, marking the second-highest single-day death toll this year.
A record-breaking 1,733 new cases were reported in the same period, the highest daily tally recorded so far in 2024.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the total number of dengue deaths in the country has now reached 157.
The total number of infections for the year has risen to 53,570 patients.
Of the new deaths, three each were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation and Chattogram division, and one each in Mymensingh and Dhaka North City Corporation.
Data shows that 63.6 percent of the total deaths recorded this year were men and 36.4 percent were women.
Earlier on September 8, the country saw its highest single-day death toll of nine people and a previous high of 1,571 hospitalisations.
